subject: Conversation amortization & trailing-token treatment — pricing impact
messages:

Subject: Conversation amortization & trailing-token treatment — pricing impact

Hi Nadia,

Quick follow from our pricing call this morning. You asked for a concise write-up on how conversation-level amortization interacts with trailing-token rounding and the practical impact on monthly invoices. I attached a short workbook that shows three examples (short burst chat, long context session, streaming transcripts) and the resulting charge delta under a few rounding/minimum policies.

High level summary:
- Amortization window: we can amortize initial prompt tokens (the "initialization" cost) across a configurable conversation horizon (we typically model 15min, 30min, 60min windows).
- Trailing tokens: tokens generated after the conversation window (e.g., follow-ups > horizon) are billed as normal and do not get amortized.
- Rounding + minimums: our billing engine currently rounds up to the nearest token and applies a per-conversation minimum (e.g., 20 tokens) for micro-requests. You asked whether we can smooth rounding across a customer's conversations within a billing period — that's not default behavior but we can propose a concession for committed customers.

Questions for you so I can put numbers into the SOW:
1) Do you expect most sessions to be short bursts (<2 minutes) or long-running (multi-turn >20 minutes)?
2) Would Helix accept a 12-month commit if we provide a temporary smoothing/credit on rounding for the first 90 days?

Next steps: if you confirm the usage profile I’ll circulate a revised SOW and a sample invoice showing the amortized vs non-amortized lines.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — very helpful summary and the workbook is useful. A couple clarifications from procurement/finance: 

- Our workload is a mix: ~60% short bursts (chat-like triage) and ~40% longer conversations (clinical note expansion where a clinician will stream a 3–8 minute audio and then ask clarifying follow-ups).
- Procurement is open to a 12-month commitment but needs an example invoice that shows how the rounding/smoothing affects our predicted monthly spend (so we can model budgets).
- A few legal constraints: any smoothing/credit needs to be auditable (line items we can show to finance), and one-off manual credits are harder for us to accept than systematic pro-rated adjustments.

Could you send a sample invoice and a short SOW redline that mentions the amortization window and minimums? Also confirm whether streaming tokens are treated differently in your engine (we have many streaming sessions).

Appreciate it — Nadia
Nadia Patel
Head of Product, Helix Health

Laura / Marissa — forwarding Nadia’s reply and the sample invoice. Procurement wants an auditable smoothing option rather than manual credits. My thought:

Proposal (internal):
- Offer a systematic pro-rated smoothing policy for rounding across the billing period for commits >= 12 months. Implementation: bill at token granularity but apply a day-level aggregation that allows fractional rounding to be accumulated and reconciled per invoice (not per-conversation).
- Pilot concession: 12% overage discount for first 3 months (applies to usage above committed baseline) in lieu of full rounding forgiveness.
- Amortization window suggestion: default 15-minute conversation horizon; allow Helix to opt for 30-minute at +5% price delta.

Risks/notes:
- Finance/legal will want the smoothing to be deterministic and visible on the invoice (we can add a "rounding-adjustment" line).
- Product/dev: implementing day-level fractional carryover is a small billing-engine change but we should scope effort.

Can we quickly commit to the pilot discount numbers and the invoice layout? If yes I’ll update the SOW and propose the DocuSign flow.

—Rishi

[In-thread quick replies:]
Marissa: agree on pilot discount but prefer 10% to start (easier margin impact) — can we do 10% for 90 days?
Dylan: engineering impact looks modest; we can add a rounding-adjustment line and a carryover bucket per billing cycle. Need formal spec.
Laura: finance prefers fixed invoice adjustments rather than post-issuance credits. If we do a discount, include it as a line item in the SOW and invoice template.

Hi Nadia —

Thanks for the profile and the call notes. Based on your mix (60/40 short/long) we ran the workbook and here is a concise proposal we can put into the SOW: 

1) Conversation amortization policy
- Default horizon: 15-minute conversation window for amortizing initial prompt tokens. Conversations reopened within 15 minutes are considered the same amortized session.
- Trailing tokens (generation after the window) are billed normally and not amortized.

2) Rounding & minimums
- Token rounding: we bill at token granularity. We will introduce a deterministic invoice line "Rounding adjustment (period carryover)" which aggregates fractional rounding across the billing period so customers can see the net effect rather than per-conversation rounding artifacts.
- Per-conversation minimum: 20 tokens minimum applies per conversation for micro-requests.

3) Pilot commercial concession
- If Helix signs a 12-month commitment we will: 
  - Apply a 10% overage discount for the first 90 days (applies to usage above committed baseline).
  - Provide an example invoice template that includes the rounding-adjustment line.

4) Streaming sessions
- Streaming input/output tokens are treated the same for billing, but streaming sessions that remain open and active will be evaluated against the 15-minute horizon for amortization; continuous streams >15 minutes will not re-amortize the initial prompt.

If that works I’ll circulate SOW_HelixHealth_v2.docx with the updated invoice example and the DocuSign link. We can also provide a month-1 invoice simulation for finance.

Action items:
- Nadia: confirm acceptance of 12-month commit + 90-day 10% pilot concession (reply ok).
- Marissa/Laura: please confirm legal/finance ok to include the rounding-adjustment deterministic line and to encode the 10% pilot in the SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Rishi
